106 THIRTY-THIRD REPORT U. S. CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION. 
EXECUTIVE ORDERS. 
General Executive orders from Oct. 31, 1914, and special exceptions to the 
civil-service rules from Oct. 5, 1914, to Sept. 14, 1915, are published in the 
Thirty-second Annual Report. The following are general orders and special 
exceptions from Sept. 15, 1915, to Aug. 31, 1916: 
I. GENERAL ORDERS AMENDING THE CIVIL SERVICE RULES. 
EXAMINATION OF ENLISTED MEN, 
April 11, 1916. 
Section 3 of Rule V of the civil-service rules, which provides that— 
3. Persons serving under enlistment shall not be examined without the writs 
ten consent of the head of the department under which they are serving— 
is hereby revoked. This action is taken in view of statements of the War 
and Navy Departments that the requirement serves no useful purpose, in 
which opinion the Civil Service Commission concurs. 
~ Enlisted men will be admitted to examinations for which they are shown to 
be eligible; the question of their discharge, if offered civil employment, will be 
determined by the military or naval authorities. 
EXCEPTION OF POSITION OF OPERATIVE, OFFICE OF AUDITOR FOR POST OFFICE 
DEPARTMENT, FROM REQUIREMENTS OF APPORTIONMENT. 
June 19, 1916. 
Civil Service Rule VII is hereby amended by adding at the end of section 2 
the following : 
“And operatives, office of the Auditor for the Post Office Department, for 
the audit of accounts and vouchers of the Postal Service by means of labor￾saving devices; and operatives so appointed shall not be eligible for transfer 
or promotion to apportioned positions or for assignment to other work.” 
The effect of this amendment will be to except from the requirement of 
apportionment the operatives described and to permit the holding of a local 
examination. The work of operatives is mechanical rather than clerical, and 
to a great extent has been done by women employees in the nonapportioned 
service transferred from the Bureau of Engraving and Printing under sec￾tion 7 of Rule X: The Secretary of the Treasury states that many persons 
appointed from the clerical registers of distant States, in accordance with the 
apportionment, have not been adapted to the work, thus occasioning em￾barrassment to the department. Operatives should be young women with 
nimble fingers who understand the Kind of work they will be called upon to 
perform and will not become dissatisfied with the work and seek transfer or 
promotion. The entrance pay is low, the work is fluctuating, and it is there￾fore desirable to appoint women from a local register of eligibles that they 
may be available as the work may require, and whose services can be ter￾minated without embarrassment. 
This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Secretary of the Treas￾ury, with the approval of the Civil Service Commission. 
REVOCATION OF AUTHORITY FOR TRANSFER OF OPERATIVES AND OTHER EMPLOYEES 
IN BUREAU OF ENGRAVING AND PRINTING TO CERTAIN POSITIONS IN OTHER PARTS 
OF TREASURY DEPARTMENT. 
June 19, 1916. 
Section 7, Civil Service Rule X, is hereby amended by striking therefrom the 
following words : 
“ Money-order assorter and skilled laborer acting as money-order assorter in 
the office of the Auditor for the Post Office Department.” 
Section 7 of Rule X permits the transfer of operatives and other employees 
in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing to certain positions in other parts of 
the department, among them those mentioned above, without examination and 
without charge to the apportionment, for the performance of certain work. 
As the audit of money orders is now done by labor-saving devices, the part of 
the rule quoted is no longer in effect.

July 8, 1916.
